content.intro: This lesson focuses on safe parsing and parser configuration and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Safe Parsing and Parser Configuration matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A YAML parser processes text into a representation and then constructs language-specific values. Parser libraries differ in API, supported version/schema, and safety defaults, so use safe loading, explicit versions, and real-target tests.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: Parsing untrusted input. Safe-loading APIs. Disabling unsafe object construction. Managing permitted tags.; Restricting resource usage. Understanding library defaults. Reviewing parser security documentation.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Safe Parsing and Parser Configuration
content_blocks.code:
import yaml
from pathlib import Path

text = Path("config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for index, document in enumerate(yaml.safe_load_all(text), start=1):
    print(index, document)
content_blocks.expected_output: With PyYAML installed and a valid multi-document stream, each document is loaded separately using the safe loader.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
